anomalies.observed: On the Power sheet the 4-pin fan headers are wired with +12V on pin 1, the tach signal (FAN_0_TACH / FAN_1_TACH) on pin 2, and GND on pin 3 (pin 4 no-connect).
anomalies.expected: The specification states the fan-header 12 V pins are pin 2 ('the two fan-header 12 V pins (J7/J8 pin 2)'), i.e. the +12V rail should land on pin 2, not pin 1. The drawing therefore places +12V, the tach line and GND on the wrong connector pins relative to the intended design.

evidence.quote: Power sheet (power.kicad_sch): J7 / J8 (Conn_01x04_Pin) — pin 1 -> +12V, pin 2 -> FAN_0_TACH / FAN_1_TACH, pin 3 -> GND, pin 4 -> NC
the two fan-header 12 V pins (J7/J8 pin 2)

anomalies.impact: A standard 4-pin fan plugged into J7/J8 would receive +12V on its GND pin and GND on its +12V pin, with the tach pin driven at +12V; the fan will not spin correctly, the tach/stall-detection input will see the wrong level (and may be damaged), and fan monitoring will not behave as intended.

parsed.summary: The board is otherwise a faithful match to the specification (all values, the power-mux, buck, heater high-side switch, SPI thermocouple channels and USB-C CC pull-downs check out), but the fan-header pinout is miswired: the drawing puts +12V on J7/J8 pin 1 whereas the spec defines the 12V pin as pin 2, swapping the supply, tach and ground lines on the connector.
